headline: Ant Group's Bailing team has released Ling-3.1-flash, an open-source AI model with about 560 billion parameters and support for very long documents.
score_reason: Notable Chinese open-source release, but the report is a short flash item mostly of the team's own figures.
importance_line: Companies that run models on their own servers get an open option for long documents that needs fewer chips, but the speed figures are from the team's own tests.
source: KuCoin News, citing Ant Group's Bailing team
summary: KuCoin News reports that Ant Group's Bailing team has open-sourced Ling-3.1-flash, a model with about 560 billion parameters in total, about 25 billion used per token, and a 1 million token context window (the amount of text it can handle at once). The team says a compression technique cut the weight storage from about 534 GB to 292 GB, so a server needs 4 chips instead of 8, though real requirements vary with workload.
notes: KuCoin flash article, which relays the team's announcement; the original announcement was not read. Article says 'yesterday', published 16 Oct 00:59 UTC.
